## Overview

The November 7, 2026 overview describes ten payment method families and routes readers to individual methods, pricing, country and currency eligibility, product support and integration options. The regional tables group methods by common use. Eligibility depends separately on the business, customer, currency, product and API. Public and private previews have limited availability. An integration can usually add another method from the same family with minimal changes. See November lines 9–48 and 165–173 and May lines 8–23 and 124–134.

## Turning on methods

When Checkout, Payment Element, Payment Links or a hosted invoice page uses dynamic payment methods, the merchant can enable most methods in the Dashboard without changing code. Stripe then displays eligible methods to each customer. An integration that lists `payment_method_types` explicitly needs a code change to add one. Check the method's individual requirements before enabling it. See November lines 13–29, [[stripe-dynamic-payment-methods]] and [[source-stripe-payment-method-integration-options]].

## Family behavior and dated regional coverage

| Family | November 7, 2026 overview |
| --- | --- |
| Cards | Global and regional card networks for online and in-person payments. The table puts Interac in-person only. Terminal brand availability varies by country and reader. The overview now describes Mexico's Meses sin intereses as a card installment example. |
| Bank debits | The merchant pulls funds from the customer's account for one-time or recurring payments. Confirmation can take several business days. Examples include ACH, Canadian pre-authorized debits, Instant Bank Payments, Bacs, SEPA and AU/NZ BECS. |
| Bank redirects | The customer authenticates with their bank and approves the payment. The regional table retains Bancontact, BLIK, EPS, FPX, iDEAL/Wero and P24, with a distinct Wero public-preview route. |
| Bank transfers | The merchant supplies a virtual bank account number. The customer pushes funds from online banking or a branch, and Stripe reconciles the transfer using that number without exposing the merchant's bank details. Examples include USD, SEPA, UK, Japan Furikomi and Mexico bank transfers. |
| Buy now, pay later | Customers pay in installments or later, and the overview describes the business as paid in full up front. It separates regional and buyer conditions, including Affirm private preview for UK businesses, Billie business customers, Kriya private preview for UK business customers, Mondu private preview for business customers and SeQura for Spanish businesses. Method and payout details remain in the individual guides. |
| Real-time payments | Customers send from a bank account or other funding source and authenticate through an intermediary. November includes Bizum, Pay by Bank and Swish (private preview) under Europe, PayNow, PayTo, PromptPay and UPI under Asia Pacific, and Pix under Latin America. |
| Stablecoin payments | A separate family. Buyers pay from a crypto wallet and completed payments settle in the business's Stripe balance in local currency. |
| Vouchers | The customer receives voucher details at checkout and pays in person at a local store, bank or other location. Listed examples include Multibanco, Konbini, Boleto and OXXO. |
| Wallets | Buyers use saved cards or stored balances. November includes TWINT here and adds Japanese private-preview entries AEON Pay, au PAY, d-Barai, Merpay and Rakuten Pay. |
| Closed-loop gift cards | Stored value redeemable with the business or a related group. The overview lists US-only private preview and settlement outside Stripe. |

See November lines 44–163.

The May 1, 2026 overview grouped eight families and listed stablecoins under wallets, Meses sin intereses under BNPL and TWINT, PayNow and UPI under bank redirects. May also listed PayNow under real-time methods, and labeled Swish invite only. In November TWINT is under wallets and PayNow and UPI under real-time methods. The separate preview Wero row appears alongside the iDEAL/Wero row. These are dated classification and coverage changes. See May lines 8–23, 49–62, 73–97 and 108–122 and November lines 57–59, 71–82, 109–126 and 137–155.

May's bank-transfer description referred to sending funds directly to the merchant's bank account. November describes the virtual account and Stripe reconciliation flow above. The captures document a change in the overview's description. Routing migration, account-specific routing and external bank payout remain separate. The May BNPL overview says paid immediately and in full, while November says paid in full up front. This wording concerns the family payment model, with bank payout timing outside its scope. See May lines 64–85 and November lines 84–107.

The May wallets table marks Apple Pay and Google Pay unavailable in India. November retains the Google Pay label and omits the Apple Pay label. The May Apple Pay method guide excludes India for customer and Stripe account locations, and its November capture is a variant index. The omission leaves eligibility unresolved. For stablecoins, the November separate method guide specifies global customer coverage excluding sanctioned countries, USD presentment with other currencies in private preview, and US businesses plus private preview for those in the European Union, Hong Kong, Mexico and Switzerland. See [[source-stripe-apple-pay]] and [[source-stripe-stablecoin-payments]].

payments-payment-methods-overview.text: Stripe then displays the eligible payment methods to each customer.
Some payment methods have additional requirements, so check the documentation for each payment method before you turn it on.
Payment methods are grouped by the regions where they’re commonly used.
Stripe uses the virtual account number to reconcile payments automatically without exposing your bank account details.
Gift card payments settle outside of Stripe.
Each payment method has its own restrictions around supported currencies, countries, products, and API options.
Customers or other businesses can use bank transfers to send money directly to your bank account

payments-payment-methods-overview.Q1: The November 7, 2026 overview at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/overview explains that a merchant can turn on most methods in the Dashboard without code changes when Checkout, Payment Element, Payment Links or hosted invoices use dynamic methods. Stripe selects eligible methods for each customer. An explicit payment_method_types integration requires code changes, and method-specific prerequisites still apply (new raw lines 13-29, 42-48). The page documents ten families. Bank debits can take several business days to confirm, bank redirects require customer authentication and approval, and bank transfers are pushed to a virtual account that Stripe reconciles. Stablecoin payments settle in the Stripe balance in local currency, while closed-loop gift cards settle outside Stripe (new raw lines 31-42, 61-86, 120-126 and 157-163). The May bank-transfer paragraph said customers or businesses sent funds directly to the merchant's bank account, while the November overview explains that the merchant supplies a virtual bank account number and Stripe reconciles the customer's bank push without exposing the merchant's account details (old raw lines 64-71 and new raw lines 84-91). The Stripe Payment Methods concept's direct bank-to-bank shorthand at line 35 is proposed for a bounded clarification. The difference in description establishes neither a routing migration nor an external bank payout. These are family-level descriptions, not individual payment object states or account eligibility. The May 1 article (old raw lines 8-23, 39-71 and 108-118) grouped eight families and lacked the explicit activation distinction and two standalone families. source-stripe-payment-methods-overview.md now dates both descriptions and separates regional use from eligibility.
payments-payment-methods-overview.Q2: The November change at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/overview contains substantive activation guidance, family additions and behavior, alongside reorganized region tables and resource navigation (new raw lines 13-42, 71-126 and 137-173). Preserve the May eight-family publication including TWINT, PayNow and UPI under Bank Redirects, stablecoins under Wallets, Meses sin intereses under BNPL, Swish invite-only, and Apple Pay and Google Pay India wording (old raw lines 8-23, 49-62, 73-97 and 108-122). November gives different placements, Wero public preview alongside a separate iDEAL | Wero link, Swish private preview, US-only private-preview gift cards, and removes only the Apple Pay India label. These table changes do not establish termination or new account eligibility. May describes transfers directly to the merchant's bank account. November describes a customer push to a virtual account reconciled by Stripe. These dated descriptions establish neither a routing migration nor an external bank payout (old raw lines 64-71 and new raw lines 84-91). Preserve the matrix distinction between regional usage and actual merchant/customer eligibility, and the scoped stablecoin business-location evidence from the separate method guide. Update source-stripe-payment-methods-overview.md with both captures and preserve root index line 7, Stripe index lines 220 and 730, and Stripe Payment Methods concept lines 88 and 92-93, adding a source backlink and keeping eligibility and integration details routed to their specific references.

concept_suggestions.anchor: Stripe supports 8 categories of payment methods, each with its own regional availability, integration pattern, and customer experience. Within a category, adding a second payment method requires minimal integration changes.
concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown: The May 1, 2026 overview groups eight payment method families. The November 7, 2026 overview lists ten, with separate stablecoin and closed-loop gift card families. The regional tables describe common use, and each method has its own eligibility and integration requirements. Adding another method in the same family usually needs minimal changes. See [[source-stripe-payment-methods-overview]].
warnings: May raw lines 8–23 and November raw lines 27–48, 120–126 and 157–163 provide taxonomy and coverage boundaries.

concept_suggestions.anchor: Direct bank-to-bank — common for large B2B payments.
concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown: Bank transfers are common for large business payments and for consumers in certain countries. The May overview describes sending funds directly to the merchant's bank account. The November overview says the merchant gives the payer a virtual account number, the payer pushes funds, and Stripe reconciles using the virtual number without exposing the merchant's account details. See [[source-stripe-payment-methods-overview]].
warnings: May raw lines 64–71 and November raw lines 84–91 describe the two dated descriptions. They do not establish a routing migration or external merchant payout.
